Bliss

Charles O’Rear’s green hill under a blue sky: the Windows XP wallpaper that made saturated nature the default view of a computer.

Context

Bliss, originally titled Bucolic Green Hills, was photographed by Charles O’Rear in January 1996 near the Napa–Sonoma county line, California, on Fujifilm Velvia. Microsoft obtained full rights in 2000 and used it as the Windows XP default wallpaper. Wikipedia: Bliss).

Avcı links the style’s nature visuals to HD-television demonstration imagery and to “the iconic ‘Bliss’ desktop wallpaper,” which “inspired many brands.” Avcı 2024, “Physical reflections of digital aesthetics”, p. 472.

Observed

  • A smooth, bright green hill fills the lower half; the grass is saturated and almost uniform.
  • The sky is a clear, deep blue that lightens toward the horizon.
  • Soft white cumulus and thin cirrus clouds cross the sky; distant hills sit low at the right.

Why it belongs

Bliss has no gloss and no interface, so it is not Frutiger Aero by itself. It is the nature half of the style in its plainest form: technology presented through a clean, saturated, human-free landscape.

Borrow

Use a real, very saturated sky-and-grass photograph as a calm backdrop behind glass panels, with no people in it.
